extracted.intended_audience: Lutheran pastors, church leaders, and denominational administrators (New York / U.S.)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for religious education, outreach to lapsed members, membership accounting, and record-keeping for Lutheran congregations (with New York-focused data and recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of membership (doctrine + practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lutheran Church's doctrine of baptism, of Christian instruction as its corollary, of repentance, faith, and the new life, of the Lord's Supper, of church attendance, of the sanctification of the Lord's Day, and a practical application of these doctrines to the life in the care of souls, establishes a standard of membership that ought to make our churches sources of spiritual power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership should be defined not merely by ritual but by doctrinal instruction and practical Christian life (attendance, sacraments, sanctified Sabbath, care of souls). Churches ought to apply these doctrines practically when defining and cultivating members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to week-day instruction in religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically and doctrinally the Lutheran Church is committed to week-day instruction in religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Week-day instruction is argued as essential because life should not be divided into secular and spiritual compartments. The church should provide systematic weekday religious instruction supplementing or coordinating with public schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunday School is insufficient for comprehensive religious education
rubrics_metrics.description: With but half an hour a week for instruction, even the best of teachers could not expect important results. Its chief value lies in the personal influence of the teacher. But instruction in religion involves more than this... it does not and cannot meet the chief requirement of the Christian school, the systematic preparation of all the children for the duties of church membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sunday School is valuable for lay activity and personal influence, but cannot replace graded, systematic, week-day religious instruction aimed at preparing children for church membership. Attendance is voluntary and doesn't reach all children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parochial schools as a means for systematic instruction (and possible consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of our churches maintain the Parochial School... Thirty churches out of one hundred and fifty... total number of pupils is 1,612... Perhaps its friends may some time see their way clear to secure greater efficiency by establishing three or four schools in place of the thirty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parochial schools can produce significant results (e.g., reportedly sending sons into the ministry) but are resource-intensive; consolidating parochial schools to serve multiple congregations may improve efficiency and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand weekday (including Saturday) instruction and confirmation classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of our churches have Saturday schools and classes in religion on other week days... total pupils reported in these classes... is 5,711. Add to these the 1,612 pupils of the parochial schools... and we have at most 7,323 children obtaining instruction in religion on week days, 17 per cent. of the number of those in attendance at Sunday School.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current provision yields only ~17% receiving weekday instruction; churches should substantially increase weekday religious instruction to reach the majority of children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid postponed and abbreviated catechization (early and sustained catechetical instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: To postpone the catechization of more than 80 per cent. of the children until they are twelve or thirteen years of age, and to complete the course of preparation for communicant membership within six months, contributes but little to the upbuilding of strong and healthy Lutheran churches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, late pre-confirmation courses undermine long-term retention; catechetical instruction should be earlier, graded, and sustained rather than compressed into a brief period immediately before confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiate school–church arrangements (excused absence for religious instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend for the favorable consideration of the Public School authorities... to allow the children to absent themselves without detriment from the public schools on Wednesday or on some other afternoon of the school week for the purpose of attending religious instruction in their own churches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue formal agreements with public schools to permit scheduled half-day/afternoon absences for church-provided religious instruction (examples: Inter-Church Conference resolution, Federal Council discussion). Be mindful of juridical limits on sectarian instruction in public schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer catechization/personal instruction over mass evangelistic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Our churches do not take kindly to the so-called evangelistic methods of reaching unchurched masses, claiming that our methods, in particular the catechization of the young, are more effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While mass evangelism is sometimes resisted, the text urges evaluating whether traditional catechetical practice is truly being implemented and suggests strengthening personal, instructive approaches rather than relying solely on episodic evangelistic campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize a systematic mobilization to reclaim lapsed Lutherans (family-based assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: These 400,000 souls may first of all be grouped in families... Let us say 90,000 families... To each church may be given an average assignment of 600 families... To an average company of 400 communicants is committed the task of evangelizing 600 families... a selective draft of 300 to do the work. The task required of each member of this army is to visit two families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, numerical plan: group lapsed members by family, assign congregations and selected communicants to visit specified numbers of families (e.g., each evangelist visits two families). Emphasizes organization, selection of workers, and feasibility within short timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Inner Mission principles for in-church evangelization
rubrics_metrics.description: Die Innere Mission... a call to personal service... recognizing the alienation of multitudes within the church... appeals to all disciples of Christ by all means to carry the Gospel to men of all classes who have strayed away and to gather them into the communion and confession of the church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Inner Mission model — mobilizing lay Christians for local, charitable, and pastoral outreach to alienated members — as a blueprint for large-scale in-church evangelization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a common standard of membership statistics (clear rubrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of statistics is greatly impaired by the absence of a common standard of membership... The Missouri Synod has three membership rubrics: souls, communicant members, voting members. The Synod of New York has three membership rubrics: Communicants, Confirmed, Baptized. The Swedish Augustana Synod has three rubrics: Communicants, Children, Total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree on and use consistent definitions (e.g., souls/baptized persons, communicants, confirmed, voting members) across congregations and synods so statistics are comparable and useful for policy and missionary planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include families and every baptized person in statistical counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Our figures should include every soul, man, woman and child, in any way related to our congregations, classified in such a way as to show clearly in what relation they stand to the church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics should record family units as well as individual relationships to the church (baptized, communicant, confirmed, excommunicated). Counting families aids pastoral planning and outreach; consider family as the basic unit in records and ministry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement accurate, up-to-date record-keeping methods
rubrics_metrics.description: I send to each family a 'Family Register' blank with spaces for the name, birthday and place of birth of each member of the family. The information thus obtained is transferred to a card catalogue... In this way, or by means of a loose-leaf record book, available and up-to-date information can easily be kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tools: Family Register blanks, card catalogues or loose-leaf records to maintain current membership rolls. Train or recruit skilled bookkeepers from congregation; consider teaching church bookkeeping in the seminary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve official records and congregational histories on durable media
rubrics_metrics.description: When important records, such as synodical minutes, are printed, several copies at least should be printed on durable paper and deposited in public libraries where they may be consulted by the historian... Congregational histories... should be sent to the public libraries of the city and of the denominational schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt archival standards: durable paper, multiple copies, deposit in public libraries and institutional repositories to ensure long-term availability for history and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove barriers to visitor inclusion and use financial engagement judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: The rented pew system, still in vogue in some congregations, is an effective means of barring out visitors... An opportunity to contribute to the church of their new neighborhood might be for them a secondary means of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exclusionary practices (e.g., rented pews) that deter visitors. Use invitations to contribute to local congregations as one practical method to re-engage people, but recognize that money alone is insufficient for full reintegration; spiritual guidance and pastoral contact are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pastoral life-event contacts to reconnect lapsed members
rubrics_metrics.description: Our office constantly brings us into association with this large outer fringe of our congregations at times when their hearts are responsive... We meet them at weddings and at funerals. We baptize their children and we bury their dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage pastoral interactions at baptisms, weddings, funerals, and other life events as opportunities for pastoral care and re-integration into the church; organize follow-up and visitation from communicants and pastors after such contacts.
